Stir in the taco seasoning, the rinsed and drained black beans and ½ cup of water and simmer until saucy, 3–4 minutes.

steps: Chop the 3 romaine hearts and divide among five big bowls. Top with the warm turkey, shredded cheddar, salsa and a spoonful of yogurt.
Crush a small handful of chips over each salad and finish with a squeeze of lime.
tips: Plain Greek yogurt does the job of sour cream here.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat the taco meat and build a fresh salad for lunch.
dinners.photo: A big taco salad of chopped romaine topped with seasoned ground turkey, black beans, shredded cheddar, salsa, a dollop of yogurt and crushed tortilla chips, with a lime wedge.

dinners.title: Sesame-ginger chicken salad
dinners.subtitle: Grilled chicken breast over romaine and crunchy cabbage with fresh orange and a sesame-ginger dressing.

steps.text: Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Lay the chicken breasts between two sheets of plastic wrap (or in a zip bag) and pound the thick ends with a rolling pin or the bottom of a pan until each is an even ¾ inch thick, so they cook through without drying out. Rub them with 1 tablespoon of the oil and 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce. Grill, turning once halfway, until marked and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press. Move to a clean plate, rest 5 minutes so the juices stay in, then slice across the grain.

steps: Whisk the remaining soy sauce and oil with the rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, grated ginger and the grated garlic clove.
Chop the 2 romaine hearts, shred the carrots and peel and segment the oranges. Toss the romaine, coleslaw mix and carrots with most of the dressing.
Divide among five bowls, top with the chicken and orange segments and drizzle with the rest of the dressing.
tips: Dress the salad right before serving so it stays crunchy.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; keep the chicken and dressing separate from the greens.
dinners.photo: A colorful salad of romaine and shredded cabbage with carrots and orange segments topped with sliced grilled chicken and a glossy sesame-ginger dressing.

dinners.title: Turkey & black bean chili
dinners.subtitle: A big pot of hearty turkey chili with beans, tomatoes and peppers, topped with cheddar and a spoonful of yogurt.

steps.text: Dice the onion and the pepper. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and cook them, stirring, until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the 2 lb of ground turkey and break it into small crumbles as it cooks, until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 165°F, 8–10 minutes.

steps: Stir in the packet of taco seasoning, the 2 cans of Bush’s chili beans with their sauce and the 2 cans of diced tomatoes with their juice. Between the packet and the beans the pot is fully seasoned.

steps.text: Bring to a boil, then turn the heat to low and simmer, partly covered and stirring now and then, until thick, 15–20 minutes. Ladle into bowls and top with shredded cheddar and a spoonful of yogurt.

tips: This is a good one for the PossibleCooker: brown the turkey on SEAR/SAUTÉ, add everything else and SLOW COOK on LO for 6 hours.
Chili is better the next day.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; freeze it flat in zip bags so it thaws quickly.
dinners.photo: A deep bowl of thick turkey and bean chili with tomatoes and peppers, topped with shredded cheddar and a dollop of yogurt.

dinners.title: Beef stroganoff noodles
dinners.subtitle: Lean ground beef and a pound of mushrooms in a creamy gravy over egg noodles.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with 2 teaspoons of the salt. Cook the 12 oz of egg noodles until tender, 6–8 minutes, drain and toss with the butter.

steps: Peel the onion and cut it into small dice. Mince the 3 garlic cloves.

steps.text: Set a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 2 lb of ground beef, the onion and the 16 oz of mushrooms and break it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon as it cooks. Keep going until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 160°F, 8–10 minutes. Keep cooking until the mushrooms are browned and their liquid has cooked off, 2–4 minutes more. Tip the pan and spoon off any liquid fat.
Stir in the garlic, flour, paprika, pepper and the remaining 1 teaspoon of salt and cook 1 minute. Pour in the 2 cups of chicken stock and simmer, stirring, until thickened to a gravy, 3–4 minutes.

steps: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sour cream and yogurt until creamy. Spoon over the noodles.
tips: Off the heat is important for the sour cream and yogurt: boiling splits them.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container. Reheat gently; boiling splits the sauce.
dinners.photo: Wide egg noodles topped with a creamy beef and mushroom stroganoff sauce, sprinkled with black pepper.

dinners.title: Bacon cheeseburger smashburgers
dinners.subtitle: Double smashed patties with a strip of crispy bacon, melted cheese, lettuce and a tangy burger sauce.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two. While it heats, stir the mayo, yogurt and ketchup with 1 tablespoon of finely chopped pickles for the burger sauce. Shred the romaine heart and divide the 2 lb of beef into 10 loose balls, a little over 3 oz each.
Crisp the 5 slices of fully cooked bacon on the griddle, about 30 seconds per side, and set them on a paper towel.

Set 5 balls on the griddle, smash each one flat and thin with a sturdy spatula and season with a pinch of the salt and pepper. Cook until the edges are deep brown and crisp, 2–3 minutes, then scrape, flip and lay a cheese slice on every other patty.
Cook 1–2 minutes more, until a thermometer slid in from the side reads 160°F. Repeat with the other 5 balls, then toast the buns cut side down on a clean part of the griddle.

steps: Spread the buns with the burger sauce and stack two patties on each with a strip of bacon, the rest of the pickles and shredded lettuce.
tips: One strip of bacon broken in half covers the whole bun.
Cold beef smashes best: keep the balls in the fridge until the griddle is hot.
dinners.leftovers: Cooked patties keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a covered skillet with a splash of water for 2–3 minutes.
dinners.photo: A double smashburger with a crispy bacon strip, melted cheddar, pickles, shredded lettuce and burger sauce on a toasted bun, plated with french fries.

dinners.title: Chicken Philly cheesesteaks
dinners.subtitle: Thin-sliced griddled chicken breast with lots of peppers and onions and melted cheese in toasted hoagie rolls.
steps: Slice the chicken breasts as thin as you can (it is easier if they are still partly frozen). Season with the garlic powder, salt and pepper. Cut the 3 peppers and the onions into thin strips.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Spread the oil on the griddle and cook the peppers and onions on one side until soft and browned, 8–10 minutes.
Cook the chicken on the other side in a thin layer, chopping and turning it with two spatulas, until no pink is left and the thickest pieces read 165°F, 5–7 minutes.
Mix the chicken and vegetables into five piles, top with the mozzarella and cover for 1 minute to melt. Spread the rolls thinly with the mayo, toast them on the griddle and scoop a pile into each.

tips: Twenty minutes in the freezer firms the chicken up enough to shave it thin.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat the filling in a skillet and toast a fresh roll.
dinners.photo: A toasted hoagie roll overflowing with thin-sliced griddled chicken, sautéed peppers and onions and gooey melted cheese.

dinners.title: Blackened Cajun chicken
dinners.subtitle: Slap Ya Mama–rubbed chicken breasts seared hard on the Blackstone and finished with a little Kerrygold.
steps: Lay the chicken breasts between two sheets of plastic wrap (or in a zip bag) and pound the thick ends with a rolling pin or the bottom of a pan until each is an even ¾ inch thick, so they cook through without drying out. Pat them dry and rub with the oil.
Season all over with the Slap Ya Mama Cajun seasoning and the smoked paprika. It is salty, so don’t add salt.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Lay the chicken on the griddle and leave it alone 5–6 minutes, until a dark, spicy crust forms and it lets go of the griddle easily.
Flip and cook 4–6 minutes more, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F. Top each piece with a small dab of the butter as it comes off, rest 5 minutes and slice.

tips: Blackened means a dark spice crust, not burnt: if it smokes hard, turn the heat down a notch.
Go lighter on the seasoning for anyone who doesn’t love heat.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; slice it for wraps or over a salad.
dinners.photo: Sliced blackened Cajun chicken breasts with a dark spice crust and melting butter on a plate beside golden Cajun diced potatoes and buttered corn.

dinners.title: Mango habanero chicken thighs
dinners.subtitle: Rubbed with Badia mango pepper, grilled, then glazed with Buffalo Wild Wings mango habanero sauce.
steps: Pat the chicken thighs dry, toss with the oil, then season both sides with the Badia mango pepper seasoning and the salt.

steps.text: Heat the electric grill (or the outdoor grill) to medium-high for 5 minutes. Grill the chicken 5–6 minutes per side, until a thermometer in the thickest thigh reads 165°F.
Brush the mango habanero sauce over both sides for the last 2 minutes, turning once, so it turns sticky without burning.

steps: Rest 5 minutes and drizzle any sauce left in the bowl over the top. It is sweet with real heat, so go light on the glaze for anyone who wants it milder.
tips: Glaze two or three thighs lightly, or not at all, for the kids.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; chop it into a rice bowl or a wrap.
dinners.photo: Grilled chicken thighs with char marks and a glossy orange mango habanero glaze, served with golden turmeric rice and steamed broccoli.

dinners.title: Chicago-style Italian beef
dinners.subtitle: Shaved roast beef soaked in a seasoned jus, piled on rolls and topped with Buona hot giardiniera.

steps.text: In a wide pot, simmer the 3 cups of chicken stock with the Italian seasoning, garlic powder, oregano, crushed red pepper and black pepper over medium heat for 5 minutes. This is the jus.
Turn the heat to low and add the shaved roast beef, pulling the slices apart. Let it soak in the hot jus until steaming and 165°F, 3–4 minutes. Don’t let it boil or the beef toughens.

steps: Split the rolls without cutting all the way through. Pile the beef in with tongs and spoon jus over each one, or dip the whole sandwich, Chicago-style.
Top with the Buona hot giardiniera and serve extra jus on the side for dipping.
tips: Giardiniera is hot: serve it on the side and let everyone add their own.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; store the beef in its jus and rewarm gently without boiling.
dinners.photo: A Chicago-style Italian beef sandwich on a long roll, juicy shaved beef topped with colorful hot giardiniera, beside fries and grilled peppers.

dinners.title: Buffalo chicken ranch wraps
dinners.subtitle: Griddled chicken tossed in Crystal hot sauce with a little butter, wrapped with lots of romaine, cheddar and Hidden Valley ranch.
steps: Cut the chicken breasts into thin strips and toss with the oil, garlic powder and salt. Chop the 2 romaine hearts.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Cook the strips in a single layer, 3–4 minutes per side, until browned and a thermometer in the thickest strip reads 165°F.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat and whisk in the Crystal hot sauce. Toss the cooked chicken in the sauce.

steps: Warm the tortillas on the griddle for 20 seconds a side. Fill each with a big handful of romaine, buffalo chicken and shredded cheddar, drizzle with the ranch and roll up tight. Two wraps per person.
tips: Toss only part of the chicken in the hot sauce if someone wants theirs plain.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; keep the chicken separate and roll fresh wraps for lunch.
dinners.photo: Two buffalo chicken wraps cut in half showing spicy orange chicken, crisp romaine, cheddar and ranch, with carrot sticks and a cup of ranch.

dinners.title: Apple-jelly glazed pork chops
dinners.subtitle: Grilled boneless chops brushed with a sweet-tangy apple jelly and mustard glaze.

steps.text: In a small saucepan over low heat, melt the apple jelly with the mustard, cider vinegar and butter, stirring until smooth. Set half aside in a clean bowl for serving.

steps: Pat the pork chops dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper.

steps.text: Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Grill the chops 4–5 minutes per side, brushing with the glaze during the last 2 minutes, until a thermometer in the center reads 145°F.
Let the chops rest 3 minutes on a clean plate, then spoon the reserved glaze over the top.

tips: Pull the chops at 145°F; lean pork dries out fast after that.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; slice thin for sandwiches.
dinners.photo: Grilled boneless pork chops with grill marks and a shiny amber apple glaze, served with a buttered sweet potato and green beans topped with crispy fried onions.

dinners.title: Cajun butter steak bites
dinners.subtitle: Lean eye of round cut into bites, seared hot and fast on the Blackstone with Slap Ya Mama and a little Kerrygold.
steps: Pat the eye of round steaks dry, trim off any silvery skin and cut the meat into 1-inch cubes.
Toss the cubes with the oil, soy sauce and Slap Ya Mama Cajun seasoning. It is salty, so don’t add salt.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on high for 10 minutes; this cut wants a very hot griddle.
Spread the steak in one layer (two batches if it is crowded) and sear without moving for 2 minutes, then turn and cook 1–2 minutes more, until a thermometer in a thick piece reads 145°F.
Push the steak together, drop the butter and black pepper on top and toss as it melts. Rest 3 minutes before serving.

tips: Eye of round is very lean, so cook it hot and fast and stop at medium; past that it turns tough.
Dry meat sears, wet meat steams: pat it well.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; slice the bites thin for steak sandwiches.
dinners.photo: Seared, glossy Cajun butter steak bites with a dark spice crust piled on a plate beside an ear of buttered corn on the cob and creamy potatoes.

dinners.title: Chorizo & nopalitos street tacos
dinners.subtitle: Lean ground beef with a little pork chorizo for flavor and tender jarred nopalitos, in Mission street taco tortillas.
steps: Drain the nopalitos in a strainer and rinse well under cold water to wash off the slippery brine, then pat dry.

steps.text: Squeeze the ½ lb of chorizo out of its casings into your largest skillet with the 1½ lb of ground beef. Cook over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 160°F, 8–10 minutes. Tip the pan and spoon off the red grease. Chorizo is fully seasoned, so nothing else goes in.
Stir in the nopalitos and cook 3–4 minutes more, until hot and catching a little color at the edges.
Warm the tortillas on the Blackstone or in a dry skillet for 20 seconds a side. Fill three per person with the chorizo and nopalitos, shredded cheese and salsa.

tips: Chorizo gives off a lot of fat; spooning it off is the difference between rich and greasy.
Out of tortillas? Spoon the filling over rice as a bowl.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container. The filling reheats well in a skillet; warm fresh tortillas to go with it.
dinners.photo: Small flour street tacos filled with crumbly red chorizo, ground beef and diced green nopalitos, topped with shredded cheese and salsa, with charro beans alongside.

dinners.title: Smoky beef & bean chili
dinners.subtitle: Lean ground beef with chili beans and fire-roasted tomatoes, seasoned with smoked paprika and Slap Ya Mama.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the 2 lb of ground beef and break it into small crumbles as it cooks, until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 160°F, 8–10 minutes.

steps: Stir in the smoked paprika and Slap Ya Mama Cajun seasoning for 30 seconds, then add the 2 cans of chili beans with their sauce and the can of diced tomatoes with its juice. The Serious Bean chipotle pintos on your shelf work as the chili beans, and a can of National Coney Island chili can go in too.

steps.text: Bring to a boil, then turn the heat to low and simmer, partly covered and stirring now and then, until thick, 15–20 minutes.

steps: Taste, then serve in bowls topped with shredded cheddar.
tips: Chili is better the next day.
It works in the PossibleCooker too: brown the beef on SEAR/SAUTÉ, add everything else and SLOW COOK on LO for 6 hours.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; freeze it flat in zip bags so it thaws quickly.
dinners.photo: A bowl of thick beef and bean chili topped with melting shredded cheddar, with buttered corn on the side.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker chicken tortilla soup
dinners.subtitle: Shredded chicken, black beans, corn and tomatoes in a mild taco-spiced broth, with cheddar, a few crushed chips and lime.
steps: Peel the onion and cut it into small dice; it cooks soft in the soup. Mince the 3 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse the 2 cans of black beans.

Put the onion, garlic, beans, the 1 lb of frozen corn, the 2 cans of diced tomatoes with their juice, the 6 cups of chicken stock, the salsa and the packet of taco seasoning in the PossibleCooker pot and stir. Lay the 2 lb of thawed chicken breasts on top and push them under the liquid.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out.

steps: Lift the chicken onto a plate. A thermometer in the thickest piece should read at least 165°F and the meat should pull apart easily. Shred it with two forks and stir it back into the soup.
Ladle into bowls and top each with shredded cheddar, a small handful of crushed tortilla chips and a squeeze of lime.
tips: Use thawed meat in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: The soup (without the chips) keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags.
dinners.photo: A wide bowl of brothy chicken tortilla soup with shredded chicken, black beans, corn and cooked tomatoes, topped with shredded cheddar, crushed tortilla chips and a lime wedge.

dinners.title: White chicken chili
dinners.subtitle: Creamy, mild chili with shredded chicken, white beans, corn and green chiles, finished with Greek yogurt and lime.
steps: Peel the onion and cut it into small dice; it cooks soft in the chili. Mince the 4 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse the 2 cans of white beans, then mash about half a can’s worth with a fork; the mashed beans thicken the chili.

Put the onion, garlic, all the beans, the 1 lb of frozen corn, the 2 small cans of mild green chiles, the 4 cups of chicken stock, the cumin, oregano and salt in the PossibleCooker pot and stir. Push the 2 lb of thawed chicken breasts under the liquid.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out.

steps: Lift the chicken onto a plate. A thermometer in the thickest piece should read at least 165°F. Shred it with two forks and stir it back in.

steps.text: Whisk a ladle of the hot broth into the yogurt in a bowl, then stir that into the pot along with the juice of the lime. Warming the yogurt first keeps it smooth. Let it stand 5 minutes with the lid on.

steps: Ladle into bowls and top with the shredded mozzarella.
tips: Canned mild green chiles add flavor, not heat; they are fine for kids.
Use thawed meat in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
dinners.leftovers: It keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags.
dinners.photo: A bowl of creamy white chicken chili with shredded chicken, white beans, corn and flecks of green chile, topped with melting shredded white cheese and a lime wedge.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker beef stew
dinners.subtitle: Lean beef simmered all day until spoon-tender with potatoes, carrots, celery and peas in a rich gravy.
steps: Cut the eye of round into 1-inch cubes and toss them in a bowl with the ¼ cup of flour, the salt and the pepper. Scrub the potatoes and cut into 1-inch chunks. Peel the carrots and cut into thick coins, slice 4 ribs of celery (half a bunch), cut the onion into chunks and mince the 3 garlic cloves.

steps.text: Take the lid off the PossibleCooker, select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to HI and press START/STOP. It preheats for about 5 minutes and beeps when it is ready for food. Add the oil, then half the beef in a single layer. Brown it 3–4 minutes, turning once, and move it to a plate. Brown the second half the same way.

Add the onion chunks and garlic to the pot and stir for 1 minute, until the onion starts to soften. Pour in the 4 cups of beef stock and scrape the browned bits off the bottom with a wooden spoon; they flavor the gravy. Press START/STOP to turn the heat off.

steps: Add the beef and its juices, the can of diced tomatoes with its juice, the Italian seasoning, the potatoes, carrots and celery, and stir.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 8 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 4 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out. The beef is ready when a piece falls apart under a spoon, far past the safe 145°F.
Stir in the 8 oz of frozen peas, put the lid back on and let them heat through for 5 minutes. Taste, add a pinch more salt if it needs it, and ladle into bowls.

tips: Browning the beef first is worth the 10 minutes: it is where the deep flavor and the gravy’s color come from.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: The stew keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags.
dinners.photo: A deep bowl of beef stew with tender chunks of beef, potatoes, carrot coins, celery and green peas in a glossy brown gravy.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker BBQ pulled chicken sandwiches
dinners.subtitle: Chicken breast slow-cooked until it shreds, tossed in a light barbecue sauce and piled on toasted buns with pickles.
steps: Peel the onion, slice it thin and spread it over the bottom of the PossibleCooker pot; it cooks down soft and sweet under the chicken. Lay the 2½ lb of thawed chicken breasts on top.
Whisk half the barbecue sauce (4 tablespoons) with the cider vinegar, the ½ cup of chicken stock, the garlic powder, paprika and salt, and pour it over the chicken.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out.

Check that a thermometer in the thickest piece reads at least 165°F. Shred the chicken right in the pot with two forks, stir in the remaining barbecue sauce and let it soak up the juices for 10 minutes with the lid on.
Toast the buns cut side down in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 1 minute. Pile them with the chicken and top with the pickles. A spoonful of the lime slaw on top is good too.

tips: Use thawed meat in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
Lift the chicken out with a slotted spoon so the buns don’t get soggy.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: The pulled chicken keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags.
dinners.photo: A toasted bun piled high with saucy shredded barbecue chicken and dill pickle chips, with creamy coleslaw and green beans on the plate.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker salsa chicken tacos
dinners.subtitle: Chicken breast slow-cooked in salsa and taco seasoning, shredded and tucked into warm corn tortillas with lettuce, cheddar and lime.
steps: Lay the 2¼ lb of thawed chicken breasts in the PossibleCooker pot. Sprinkle the packet of taco seasoning over them and pour the 16 oz of salsa on top. The salsa is all the liquid it needs.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out.

Check that a thermometer in the thickest piece reads at least 165°F. Shred the chicken in the pot with two forks and stir it into the salsa juices. Let it stand 5 minutes with the lid on to soak them up.

Warm the street-taco tortillas two or three at a time in a dry skillet over medium-high heat, 20–30 seconds per side, until soft with a few toasted spots. Stack them inside a clean kitchen towel so they stay warm and bendy.

steps: Shred the romaine heart and the cheddar. Fill three tortillas per person with chicken, lettuce and cheese, and finish with a spoonful of yogurt and a squeeze of lime.
tips: Use thawed meat in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
Use a slotted spoon to fill the tacos so they don’t drip.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: The shredded chicken keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags. It makes quick quesadillas and rice bowls.
dinners.photo: Corn tortilla street tacos filled with juicy shredded salsa chicken, shredded lettuce and cheddar, with a dollop of yogurt and lime wedges.

dinners.title: Braised pork loin with apples & onions
dinners.subtitle: Lean pork loin seared and gently braised with soft apples and onions, sliced and served with a cider-mustard pan sauce.
steps: Trim the white fat cap off the 2¼ lb piece of pork loin, pat the meat dry and season all over with the salt, pepper and Italian seasoning. Peel the onions and cut into thick half-moons. Core the apples and cut each into 8 wedges, peel on. Mince the 3 garlic cloves.

steps.text: Take the lid off the PossibleCooker, select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to HI and press START/STOP. It preheats for about 5 minutes and beeps when it is ready for food. Add the oil and the pork and brown it 2–3 minutes on each of its four sides, 8–10 minutes in all. Move it to a plate.

Add the onions to the pot and cook, stirring, until soft and golden, 4–5 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in the 1½ cups of chicken stock, the cider vinegar and the mustard and scrape the browned bits off the bottom with a wooden spoon. Press START/STOP to turn the heat off.

Set the pork back in the pot with its juices and tuck the apple wedges around it. Put the lid on, select BRAISE, set the time to 45 minutes and press START/STOP. It is done when a thermometer pushed into the center of the pork reads 145°F; if it is not there yet, give it 5–10 minutes more.
Move the pork to a cutting board and rest it at least 3 minutes (10 is better) so the juices stay in.

While it rests, stir the cornstarch into 1 tablespoon of cold water. Select SEAR/SAUTÉ on MED, stir the cornstarch into the pot and simmer until the sauce turns glossy, 1–2 minutes. Slice the pork ½ inch thick across the grain and serve with the apples, onions and sauce.

tips: A thermometer is the whole secret with lean pork: pull it at 145°F and it stays juicy, with a hint of pink.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge in a covered container; slice it thin for sandwiches, or reheat slices gently in the sauce.
dinners.photo: Thick slices of juicy pork loin fanned on a platter with soft golden apple wedges and cooked onions, spooned with a glossy cider-mustard pan sauce.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker chicken noodle soup
dinners.subtitle: Shredded chicken, carrots, celery and egg noodles in a golden broth with a squeeze of lemon.
steps: Peel the carrots and cut into coins, slice 4 ribs of celery (half a bunch), peel the onion and cut it into small dice, and mince the 3 garlic cloves.

steps.text: Take the lid off the PossibleCooker, select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to MED and press START/STOP. It preheats for about 5 minutes and beeps when it is ready for food. Add the oil, onion, carrots and celery and cook, stirring, until the onion is soft and see-through, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds. Press START/STOP to turn the heat off.

steps: Pour in the 8 cups of chicken stock (two cartons), add the Italian seasoning, salt and pepper, and push the 2 lb of thawed chicken breasts under the liquid.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out.

steps: Lift the chicken onto a plate. A thermometer in the thickest piece should read at least 165°F. Shred it with two forks.

steps.text: Take the lid off, select SEAR/SAUTÉ on HI and bring the soup to a gentle boil, about 8 minutes. Add the 6 oz of egg noodles (half a 12 oz bag) and the 6 oz of frozen peas and cook until the noodles are tender, 6–8 minutes. Stir the chicken back in, squeeze in the juice of the lemon and press START/STOP.

tips: Cook the noodles at the end, in the hot broth: noodles that slow-cook all day turn to mush.
Use thawed meat in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; the noodles keep soaking up broth, so add a splash of water when you reheat. To freeze, freeze it before the noodles go in.
dinners.photo: A bowl of chicken noodle soup with shredded chicken, wide egg noodles, carrot coins, celery and peas in a clear golden broth, a lemon wedge beside it.

dinners.title: Turkey meatballs in marinara
dinners.subtitle: Tender lean turkey meatballs simmered right in the marinara with spinach, served over spaghetti with Parmesan.
steps: In a large bowl mix the 2 lb of ground turkey with the panko, the egg, half the Parmesan, the garlic powder, the Italian seasoning and 1 teaspoon of the salt. Mix with your hands only until it comes together. With wet hands, roll it into 25 meatballs about 1½ inches across.

Pour the jar of Rao’s marinara, the can of diced tomatoes with its juice and ½ cup of water into the PossibleCooker pot and stir. Set the meatballs into the sauce in a single layer and spoon a little sauce over each.

steps.text: Put the lid on, select BRAISE, set the time to 40 minutes and press START/STOP. Leave them alone for the first 20 minutes so they firm up, then turn each one gently with a wooden spoon. They are done when a thermometer in the center of a meatball reads 165°F.

When the meatballs have about 25 minutes left, fill your largest pot with about 5 quarts of water, add 1 tablespoon of the salt, cover and bring it to a full rolling boil on the stove over high heat. It takes 10–15 minutes.

Add the 10 oz of spaghetti (a little over half a 1 lb box) to the boiling water, stir for the first minute so it doesn’t stick, and boil uncovered until tender with a little bite, 9–11 minutes (check the box). Drain.
Stir the 5 oz of spinach into the sauce around the meatballs and put the lid back on for 2 minutes, until it wilts. Serve the meatballs and sauce over the spaghetti with the rest of the Parmesan.

tips: No browning needed: simmering the meatballs in the sauce keeps lean turkey tender and saves a pan.
Don’t pack the meatballs tight; a light hand keeps them soft.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
dinners.leftovers: Meatballs in sauce keep 4 days in the fridge and freeze for 3 months; they make good hoagies with a little mozzarella.
dinners.photo: A plate of spaghetti topped with round turkey meatballs in a chunky red marinara with wilted spinach and grated Parmesan.

dinners.title: Turkey sausage minestrone
dinners.subtitle: A big pot of vegetable soup with lean turkey Italian sausage, white beans, carrots, zucchini, spinach and little pasta.
steps: Peel the carrots and cut into small dice, slice 4 ribs of celery (half a bunch), peel the onion and cut it into small dice, and mince the 3 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse the 2 cans of white beans.

steps.text: Take the lid off the PossibleCooker, select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to HI and press START/STOP. It preheats for about 5 minutes and beeps when it is ready for food. Add the oil and squeeze the 1½ lb of turkey Italian sausage out of its casings into the pot. Cook, breaking it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon, until no pink is left and it reads 165°F, 8–10 minutes.
Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook, stirring, until the onion is soft, 4–5 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds, then press START/STOP to turn the heat off.

steps: Pour in the 6 cups of chicken stock and add the 2 cans of diced tomatoes with their juice, the beans, the Italian seasoning and the salt. Stir.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out.

Cut the zucchini into half-moons. Take the lid off, select SEAR/SAUTÉ on HI and bring the soup to a gentle boil, about 8 minutes. Add the zucchini and the 6 oz of elbow macaroni and cook until the pasta is tender, 8–10 minutes. Stir in the 5 oz of spinach until it wilts and press START/STOP.

steps: Ladle into bowls and top with the Parmesan.
tips: The pasta and zucchini go in at the end so they keep their shape.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; add a splash of water when reheating because the pasta drinks the broth. To freeze, freeze it before the pasta goes in.
dinners.photo: A hearty bowl of minestrone with crumbled sausage, white beans, diced carrots, zucchini half-moons, elbow pasta and wilted spinach in a tomato broth, topped with grated Parmesan.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker sesame-ginger chicken
dinners.subtitle: Chicken thighs and carrots slow-cooked in soy, ginger and garlic until they fall apart, in a glossy sesame sauce.
steps: Peel the 1 lb of carrots and cut into ½-inch coins. Mince the 4 garlic cloves and grate the ginger. Whisk the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger and the ½ cup of chicken stock in a bowl.
Spread the carrots over the bottom of the PossibleCooker pot, lay the 2½ lb of thawed chicken thighs on top and pour the sauce over everything.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out.

steps: Lift the chicken onto a plate. A thermometer should read at least 165°F and the meat should fall apart. Pull it into big shreds with two forks.

steps.text: Stir the cornstarch into 2 tablespoons of cold water. Take the lid off, select SEAR/SAUTÉ on HI, stir the cornstarch into the juices and simmer until the sauce is glossy and coats a spoon, 2–3 minutes. Press START/STOP, stir the chicken back in and drizzle with the sesame oil.

tips: Start the rice about 30 minutes before you want to eat.
Use thawed meat in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: The chicken in its sauce keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags.
dinners.photo: A bowl of white jasmine rice topped with shredded chicken thighs and carrot coins in a glossy brown sesame-ginger sauce, with steamed broccoli alongside.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker beef & broccoli
dinners.subtitle: Thin strips of lean beef slow-cooked tender in a garlic-ginger soy sauce, finished with two pounds of broccoli.
steps: Slice the eye of round across the grain into thin strips, about ¼ inch thick; it is much easier while the meat is still a little frozen. Mince the 4 garlic cloves and grate the ginger.
Stir the cup of beef stock, the soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic and ginger together in the PossibleCooker pot. Add the beef and stir so every strip is in the sauce.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out. The beef is ready when a strip pulls apart easily, far past the safe 145°F.

Stir the cornstarch into 3 tablespoons of cold water and stir it into the pot. Add the 2 lb of frozen broccoli on top. Select SEAR/SAUTÉ on HI, put the lid on and cook until the broccoli is hot and bright green and the sauce has thickened, 8–10 minutes, stirring once halfway. Press START/STOP.

steps: Drizzle with the sesame oil and serve.
tips: Cut across the grain (across the lines in the meat): short fibers are what make lean beef tender.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge in a covered container; it reheats well in the microwave and is good over rice or noodles.
dinners.photo: A bowl of tender sliced beef and bright green broccoli florets in a glossy dark garlic-ginger soy sauce, with golden potstickers on the side.

dinners.title: One-pot lasagna soup
dinners.subtitle: Everything good about lasagna in a bowl: lean turkey, marinara, penne and spinach under melting mozzarella and Parmesan.
steps: Peel the onion and cut it into small dice. Mince the 3 garlic cloves.

steps.text: Take the lid off the PossibleCooker, select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to HI and press START/STOP. It preheats for about 5 minutes and beeps when it is ready for food. Add the oil, the 2 lb of ground turkey and the onion. Cook, breaking the turkey into small crumbles with a wooden spoon, until no pink is left, the onion is soft and the meat reads 165°F, 8–10 minutes. Stir in the garlic and Italian seasoning for 30 seconds.
Pour in the jar of Rao’s marinara, the can of diced tomatoes with its juice, the 5 cups of chicken stock and the salt. Put the lid on and bring it to a boil, about 8 minutes.
Take the lid off, stir in the 8 oz of penne (half a 1 lb box) and boil gently, stirring every couple of minutes so nothing sticks, until the pasta is tender, 11–13 minutes.

steps: Press START/STOP to turn the heat off and stir in the 6 oz of spinach until it wilts. Ladle into bowls and top each with mozzarella and Parmesan; the heat of the soup melts them.
tips: The soup thickens as it stands. Loosen leftovers with a splash of stock or water.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge in a covered container; add a splash of water when reheating because the pasta drinks the broth.
dinners.photo: A bowl of thick tomato lasagna soup with penne, crumbled ground turkey and wilted spinach, topped with melting mozzarella and grated Parmesan.

dinners.title: Braised chicken cacciatore
dinners.subtitle: Chicken thighs braised with peppers, mushrooms, onions and tomatoes until tender, spooned over egg noodles.
steps: Pat the chicken thighs dry and season with 1½ teaspoons of the salt and the pepper. Cut the 3 peppers and the onion into strips and mince the 4 garlic cloves.

steps.text: Take the lid off the PossibleCooker, select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to HI and press START/STOP. It preheats for about 5 minutes and beeps when it is ready for food. Add the oil and half the chicken and brown it about 3 minutes per side; it finishes cooking in the sauce. Move it to a plate and brown the rest.

Add the peppers, onion strips and the 8 oz of mushrooms to the pot and cook, stirring, until soft, 5–6 minutes. Stir in the garlic and Italian seasoning for 30 seconds. Add the 2 cans of diced tomatoes with their juice and the ½ cup of chicken stock and scrape the browned bits off the bottom. Press START/STOP to turn the heat off.

Tuck the chicken and its juices into the sauce. Put the lid on, select BRAISE, set the time to 35 minutes and press START/STOP. The chicken is done when a thermometer in the thickest thigh reads at least 165°F and the meat is fork-tender.
When the braise has 15 minutes left, bring a large pot of water to a boil on the stove with the remaining 1 teaspoon of salt. Cook the 10 oz of egg noodles until tender, 6–8 minutes, and drain.

steps: Serve the chicken, vegetables and sauce over the noodles.
tips: Thighs are forgiving: unlike breasts, they only get more tender if the braise runs a few minutes long.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
dinners.leftovers: The chicken and sauce (without the noodles) keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags.
dinners.photo: Braised chicken thighs in a chunky tomato sauce with soft strips of bell pepper, mushrooms and cooked onion, served over wide egg noodles.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker Italian beef
dinners.subtitle: Lean beef slow-cooked all day in a garlicky Italian jus, shredded and piled on rolls with sweet peppers and hot giardiniera.
steps: Stir the 3 cups of beef stock with the Italian seasoning, garlic powder, oregano, crushed red pepper, black pepper and salt in the PossibleCooker pot. Add the eye of round steaks and turn them so they are covered.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 8 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 4 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out. The beef is ready when it pulls apart with a fork, far past the safe 145°F.

steps: Lift the beef onto a cutting board and pull it into thin shreds with two forks, or slice it as thin as you can across the grain. Cut the 2 peppers into strips.

steps.text: Return the beef to the jus with the pepper strips. Select SEAR/SAUTÉ on MED, put the lid on and simmer until the peppers are soft, about 10 minutes. Press START/STOP.

steps: Split the rolls without cutting all the way through. Pile in the beef and peppers with tongs and spoon jus over each one, or dip the whole sandwich, Chicago-style. Top with the Buona hot giardiniera for anyone who likes heat, and serve extra jus for dipping.
tips: Eye of round is the classic lean cut for Italian beef; the long, slow cook is what makes it tender.
Use thawed meat in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: The beef in its jus keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags. Rewarm it gently without boiling.
dinners.photo: A Chicago-style Italian beef sandwich on a long roll, juicy shredded beef and soft cooked sweet pepper strips topped with colorful hot giardiniera, a cup of jus beside it.

sides.title: Air-fryer fries
steps: Use one 26 oz bag of frozen fries (fast-food style, shoestring or curly all work), picking a bag with air-fryer directions on the package.

steps.text: Heat the air fryer to the package temperature (usually 400°F). Cook the fries from frozen in single layers, shaking the basket halfway, until crisp and golden, about 12–18 minutes per batch.

steps: Toss with the salt while hot. Tent finished batches loosely with foil while the rest cook, then serve right away.
tips: Fries crisp in a single layer; an overfilled basket steams them soft.
sides.photo: A generous heap of golden, crispy straight-cut french fries lightly sprinkled with salt in a paper-lined basket.

sides.title: Steamed broccoli with butter
steps: Bring about ½ inch of water to a boil in a large saucepan over high heat.

steps.text: Add the 1½ lb of frozen broccoli, cover and steam over medium heat until bright green and tender-crisp, 5–7 minutes.

steps: Drain well, toss with the butter and salt, and serve.
sides.photo: A bowl of bright green steamed broccoli florets glistening with melted butter.

sides.title: Creamy lime slaw
steps: Zest and juice the lime into a large bowl. Whisk in the yogurt, honey, salt and 1 tablespoon of water until smooth.
Add the coleslaw mix and toss until evenly coated.
Chill until serving (up to 2 hours) and toss again before serving.
sides.photo: A bowl of creamy shredded green and purple cabbage slaw with carrot strands and flecks of lime zest.

sides.title: Chopped romaine salad
steps: Chop the 2 romaine hearts, rinse, spin or pat dry, and put them in a large bowl.
Whisk the juice of the lemon with the oil, salt and pepper.
Toss the salad with the dressing just before serving so it stays crisp.
sides.photo: A large bowl of crisp chopped romaine lettuce, nothing but romaine, glossy with a light lemon vinaigrette and cracked black pepper, a halved lemon beside the bowl.

sides.title: Buttered peas
steps: Bring ½ cup of water to a boil in a saucepan, add the frozen peas and cover.
Simmer until hot and tender, 3–4 minutes, then drain.
Stir in the butter and salt and serve warm.
sides.photo: A bowl of bright green sweet peas shining with melted butter.

sides.title: Buttered green beans
steps: Drain the green beans and put them in a saucepan with 2 tablespoons of water.
Cover and heat over medium, stirring once or twice, until steaming, 4–5 minutes. Drain off any liquid.
Toss with the butter and black pepper and serve.
sides.photo: A bowl of tender cut green beans glossy with butter and cracked black pepper.

sides.title: Buttered sweet corn
steps: Drain the corn and put it in a saucepan with the butter.
Heat over medium, stirring, until hot and the butter coats every kernel, 3–4 minutes.
Season with the pepper and serve.
sides.photo: A bowl of golden buttered sweet corn kernels.

sides.title: Honey-glazed carrots
steps: Drain the sliced carrots well.
Melt the butter with the honey in a skillet over medium heat, add the carrots and cook, stirring gently, until hot and glazed, 4–5 minutes.
sides.photo: A bowl of shiny honey-glazed sliced carrot coins.

sides.title: Seasoned black beans
steps: Rinse and drain the black beans and put them in a saucepan with the taco seasoning and ¼ cup water.
Simmer over medium, stirring, until hot and slightly thickened, 4–5 minutes.
Squeeze the lime over the top and serve.
sides.photo: A bowl of warm seasoned black beans with a lime wedge.

sides.title: Grilled peppers & onions
steps: Quarter the 3 peppers and cut the onions into thick rounds. Brush with the oil and sprinkle with the salt.

steps.text: Grill on the preheated electric grill, turning once, until tender and charred at the edges and the onions are soft all the way through, 8–10 minutes.

steps: Slice into strips and serve warm.
sides.photo: Charred strips of red, yellow and green bell peppers and grilled onion rings with grill marks on a platter.

sides.title: Carrot sticks & ranch
steps: Scrub or peel the 1¼ lb of carrots, trim the ends and cut into sticks.
Divide among five plates with a small spoonful of ranch for dipping.
sides.photo: Bright orange carrot sticks arranged around a small bowl of creamy ranch dip.

sides.title: Crisp apple slices
steps: Wash and core the apples.
Slice just before serving so they stay bright, and divide among five plates.
sides.photo: Fanned slices of crisp red and green apples on a small plate.

sides.title: Fresh orange wedges
steps: Scrub the oranges under running water.
Cut each into 8 wedges and divide among five plates.
sides.photo: Juicy navel orange wedges arranged on a white plate.

sides.title: Air-fryer potato wedges
steps: Scrub the 2 lb of potatoes and cut into slim wedges. Toss with the oil, salt, paprika and garlic powder until evenly coated.

steps.text: Heat the air fryer to 390°F. Cook the wedges in single layers, shaking the basket halfway, until tender inside and browned outside, 18–22 minutes per batch.

steps: Tent finished batches with foil while the rest cook.
tips: Soaking the cut wedges in cold water for 10 minutes and drying them well makes them crisper.
sides.photo: Golden crispy seasoned potato wedges with browned edges piled in a bowl.

sides.title: Cinnamon-butter sweet potatoes
steps: Scrub the sweet potatoes and pierce each several times with a fork.
Microwave on a plate in batches, turning halfway, until a knife slides easily into the centers, 8–15 minutes per batch depending on size.
Split open and top with the butter, a pinch of salt and a light dusting of the ground cinnamon.
sides.photo: Split sweet potatoes with bright orange fluffy flesh topped with melting butter.

sides.title: Warm naan
steps: Heat a large dry skillet over medium heat.

steps.text: Warm each of the 3 naan 30–60 seconds per side, until soft with a few golden spots.

steps: Brush lightly with the butter and cut each into 5 wedges: three wedges a plate.
sides.photo: Warm, golden-spotted naan flatbreads brushed with butter and cut into wedges in a basket.

sides.title: Garlic toast
steps: Soften the butter and stir in the 2 minced garlic cloves.
Spread it thinly over one side of each of the 5 bread slices.

steps.text: Air-fry buttered side up at 370°F in single layers until golden and crisp at the edges, 3–5 minutes per batch. Cut each slice in half.

sides.photo: Golden, crisp slices of garlic butter toast cut into halves on a board.

sides.title: Grilled honey apples
steps: Core the apples and cut into thick wedges. Brush lightly with the oil.
Grill on a clean electric grill until marked and just tender, 3–4 minutes per side.
Drizzle with the honey and serve warm.
sides.photo: Thick apple wedges with golden grill marks drizzled with honey on a plate.

sides.title: Creamy tomato soup
steps: Combine the jar of Rao’s marinara (already fully seasoned, so no herbs are needed) and the 2 cups of chicken stock in a saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring.

steps.text: Simmer gently 10 minutes so the flavors blend.

steps: Turn the heat to low, stir in the milk and heat until steaming (don’t let it boil). Ladle into five mugs or bowls.
sides.photo: A mug of smooth, creamy orange-red tomato soup with a swirl on top.

sides.title: Buttery smashed potatoes
steps: Scrub the 2¼ lb of potatoes and cut into 1½-inch chunks (skins on). Put them in a pot, cover with cold water and add half the salt.

steps.text: Bring to a boil and simmer until a fork slides in easily, 12–15 minutes. Drain and return to the pot.

steps: Smash with the butter, milk, remaining salt and the pepper, leaving them a little chunky.
sides.photo: A bowl of rustic, buttery smashed gold potatoes with skins, topped with a melting pat of butter and black pepper.

sides.title: Warm lemon chickpeas
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas and pat dry.
Warm the oil in a skillet over medium, add the chickpeas and minced garlic and cook, stirring, until hot and lightly golden, 4–5 minutes.
Off the heat, toss with the oregano, salt and the juice of the lemon.
sides.photo: A bowl of golden warm chickpeas tossed with lemon, garlic and oregano.

sides.title: Garlic green beans

steps.text: Trim the 1½ lb of green beans. Bring ½ inch of water to a boil in a large skillet, add the beans, cover and steam until bright green and crisp-tender, 4–5 minutes. Drain the skillet.
Add the oil and butter to the skillet over medium-high heat and cook the beans, tossing, until blistered in spots, 3–4 minutes.

steps: Add the 3 minced garlic cloves and the salt and toss 30 seconds, until fragrant. Serve right away.
sides.photo: A platter of blistered fresh green beans tossed with golden sliced garlic and butter.

sides.title: Buttered corn on the cob
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Add the frozen mini ears and cook until hot and tender, 6–8 minutes (or as the package directs).
Drain, roll in the butter and sprinkle with the salt. Two ears per person.
sides.photo: Golden mini ears of sweet corn on the cob glistening with melted butter and flaky salt.

sides.title: Cilantro-lime rice
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Combine with 2¼ cups water and the salt in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 minutes. Rest, covered, 10 minutes off the heat.
Fluff with a fork and fold in the butter, the zest and juice of the lime and the chopped cilantro.
sides.photo: A bowl of fluffy white jasmine rice flecked with chopped green cilantro and lime zest, with a lime wedge.

sides.title: Steamed jasmine rice
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Combine with 2¼ cups water and the salt in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 minutes.
Rest, covered, 10 minutes off the heat, then fluff with a fork.
sides.photo: A neat mound of fluffy steamed white jasmine rice in a bowl.

sides.title: Stovetop mac & cheese
steps: Boil the macaroni in a pot of water with the salt until just tender, 7–8 minutes. Drain and return to the pot.
Whisk the cornstarch into the cold milk, pour it over the pasta with the butter and stir over medium-low heat until the milk thickens, 2–3 minutes.
Take off the heat and stir in the shredded cheddar until smooth and creamy.
sides.photo: A bowl of creamy, cheesy elbow macaroni with a glossy golden cheddar sauce.

sides.title: Sesame-ginger slaw
steps: Shred the carrot and toss it with the coleslaw mix in a large bowl.
Whisk the rice vinegar, sesame oil, soy sauce, honey and grated ginger.
Toss the slaw with the dressing and let stand 10 minutes before serving.
sides.photo: A bowl of crunchy shredded cabbage and carrot slaw glossy with sesame-ginger dressing.

sides.title: Sesame edamame
steps: Bring a saucepan of water to a boil, add the frozen edamame and cook until hot and tender, 4–5 minutes.
Drain and toss with the sesame oil and salt.
sides.photo: A bowl of bright green shelled edamame beans glistening with sesame oil and flaky salt.

sides.title: Crispy potstickers

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 15 frozen potstickers flat side down and cook until the bottoms are golden, about 2 minutes.
Carefully add ½ cup of water (it spatters), cover right away and steam until the water is gone and the filling is hot, 6–8 minutes (follow the package if it differs).

steps: Uncover and cook 1 minute more to re-crisp. Stir the soy sauce and rice vinegar together for dipping. Three per person.
sides.photo: Golden pan-fried potstickers with crispy browned bottoms arranged on a plate with a small bowl of soy dipping sauce.

sides.title: Air-fryer zucchini & peppers
steps: Cut the zucchini into half-moons and the 2 peppers and the onion into 1-inch pieces.
Toss with the oil, Italian seasoning, garlic powder and salt.

steps.text: Air-fry at 400°F in single layers, shaking halfway, until tender and browned at the edges and the onion is soft, 10–14 minutes per batch.

sides.photo: Browned zucchini half-moons with red and yellow bell pepper pieces and soft browned onion on a platter.

sides.title: Applesauce cups
steps: Chill the applesauce cups and set one at each plate.
sides.photo: A small glass dish of smooth golden applesauce.

sides.title: Chilled pineapple chunks
steps: Chill the cans ahead of time if you can.
Drain the pineapple chunks and divide among five small bowls.
sides.photo: A bowl of juicy golden pineapple chunks.

sides.title: Smoky pork & beans
steps: Empty the pork and beans into a saucepan and stir in the barbecue sauce and mustard.

steps.text: Simmer over medium-low heat, stirring often, until thick and bubbling, 8–10 minutes.

sides.photo: A bowl of thick, saucy barbecue-style beans in a glossy brown sauce.

sides.title: Tortilla chips & salsa
steps: Pour the chips into a bowl (about a handful each) and the salsa into a smaller one for dipping.
sides.photo: A basket of golden tortilla chips beside a small bowl of smooth red jarred salsa.

sides.title: Cajun skillet potatoes
steps: Drain the Del Monte Cajun-style diced potatoes well and pat them dry so they brown instead of steam.
Melt the butter in your largest skillet over medium-high. Spread the potatoes in one layer and cook 8–10 minutes, stirring only every few minutes, until browned and crisp at the edges.
They’re already seasoned, so taste before adding any salt.
sides.photo: Golden, crisp-edged diced Cajun potatoes flecked with red pepper and spices in a cast-iron skillet.

sides.title: Golden turmeric rice
steps: Rinse the 1½ cups of basmati rice in a strainer until the water runs mostly clear.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the turmeric for 30 seconds, then add the rice, 2¼ cups of water and the salt. Bring to a boil.

steps.text: Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer 15 minutes without lifting the lid. Rest 5 minutes with the lid on, then fluff with a fork. Short on time? Microwave basmati rice pouches and stir in the turmeric butter instead.

sides.photo: A bowl of fluffy golden-yellow turmeric basmati rice with separate long grains and a small pat of butter.

sides.title: Old Bay air-fryer fries
steps: Air-fry one 26 oz bag of frozen fries from frozen at the package temperature (usually 400°F) in single layers, shaking the basket halfway, until crisp and golden, about 12–18 minutes per batch.
Toss the hot fries in a big bowl with the Old Bay seasoning. It’s salty, so skip any other salt.
sides.photo: Crispy golden french fries dusted with reddish Old Bay-style seasoning in a paper-lined basket.

sides.title: Cajun air-fryer fries
steps: Air-fry one 26 oz bag of frozen fries from frozen at the package temperature (usually 400°F) in single layers, shaking the basket halfway, until crisp and golden, about 12–18 minutes per batch.
Toss the hot fries with the Slap Ya Mama Cajun seasoning right away so it sticks. It’s salty, so skip any other salt.
sides.photo: Crispy french fries tossed with orange-red Cajun spice seasoning in a metal basket lined with paper.

sides.title: Green beans with crispy onions
steps: Drain the canned green beans and warm them with the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, 4–5 minutes.
Season with the black pepper, pour into a serving bowl and scatter the French’s crispy fried onions over the top right before serving so they stay crunchy.
sides.photo: A serving bowl of buttered green beans topped with a crunchy pile of golden crispy fried onions.

sides.title: Charro beans
steps: Empty the La Preferida charro beans and their broth into a saucepan.
Warm over medium, stirring now and then, until bubbling, 6–8 minutes. They’re already seasoned, so nothing else goes in.
sides.photo: A bowl of brothy Mexican charro beans: pinto beans simmered with bits of bacon and jalapeño in a light tomato broth.

sides.title: Steamed carrots with butter
steps: Peel the 1½ lb of carrots and cut into ½-inch coins.

steps.text: Pour 1 cup of water into the PossibleCooker pot, add the carrots and put the lid on. Select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to HI and press START/STOP. Once steam is coming from under the lid (about 5 minutes), cook 8–10 minutes more, until a fork slides into a coin easily. Press START/STOP.

steps: Drain well, toss with the butter and salt, and serve.
tips: If your panel has a STEAM button, use it with the same water and time; SEAR/SAUTÉ with the lid on steams just as well on every model.
sides.photo: A bowl of bright orange steamed carrot coins glistening with a little melted butter.

sides.title: Steamed green beans with lemon
steps: Trim the stem ends off the 1½ lb of green beans.

steps.text: Pour 1 cup of water into the PossibleCooker pot, add the beans and put the lid on. Select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to HI and press START/STOP. Once steam is coming from under the lid (about 5 minutes), cook 6–8 minutes more, until they are bright green and bend without snapping. Press START/STOP.

steps: Drain well and toss with the butter, the salt and the juice of half the lemon. Cut the other half into wedges for the table.
tips: If your panel has a STEAM button, use it with the same water and time; SEAR/SAUTÉ with the lid on steams just as well on every model.
sides.photo: A platter of bright green steamed whole green beans glistening with butter, with lemon wedges.

sides.title: PossibleCooker jasmine rice
steps: Rinse the 1½ cups of jasmine rice in a fine strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.

steps.text: Put the rice, the salt and 2¼ cups of water in the PossibleCooker pot. (Ninja’s ratio is 1½ cups of water for each cup of white rice; the lines inside the pot mark it for whole cups.) Put the lid on, select WHITE RICE and press START/STOP. The cooker sets the time itself, about 25 minutes, and switches to KEEP WARM when the rice is done.

steps: Fluff with the rice paddle and serve.
tips: It holds on KEEP WARM until everything else is ready, which makes it the easy way to time a rice dinner.
sides.photo: A neat mound of fluffy steamed white jasmine rice in a bowl with a rice paddle.

sides.title: Steamed mixed vegetables
steps: Bring about ½ inch of water to a boil in a large saucepan over high heat.

steps.text: Add the 1½ lb of frozen mixed vegetables, cover and steam over medium heat until hot and tender, 5–7 minutes.

steps: Drain well and toss with the butter, salt and pepper.
sides.photo: A bowl of steamed mixed vegetables (peas, corn, diced carrots and cut green beans) glistening with a little butter.

sides.title: Spinach & apple salad
steps: Whisk the juice of the lemon with the oil, honey, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Core the apples and slice them thin. Toss them in the dressing right away so they stay bright.
Add the 6 oz of baby spinach and toss just before serving.
sides.photo: A bowl of fresh baby spinach tossed with thin slices of crisp red apple in a light lemon dressing.

sides.title: Lighter mashed potatoes
steps: Peel the 2¼ lb of potatoes and cut into 1-inch chunks.

steps.text: Put the potatoes in the PossibleCooker pot with enough cold water to just cover them (about 6 cups) and half the salt. Put the lid on, select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to HI and press START/STOP. It comes to a boil in about 12 minutes.
Set the lid a little ajar and boil gently until a chunk falls apart under a fork, 12–15 minutes. Press START/STOP.

steps: Lift the pot out by its handles with pot holders and drain the potatoes in a colander, then tip them back into the pot. Mash with a silicone or wooden masher (the pot is nonstick) and stir in the ½ cup of chicken stock, the yogurt, butter, pepper and the rest of the salt until creamy.
tips: Yogurt and a little stock make them creamy with a quarter of the usual butter.
Warm the stock for 30 seconds in the microwave so the potatoes stay hot.
sides.photo: A bowl of creamy mashed potatoes with a small pat of melting butter and cracked black pepper.
